A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FMA-Net++ research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments, benchmark comparisons, component ablations and qualitative results on synthetic and real-world videos.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds controlled exposure-conditioning comparisons, guidance-corruption experiments and quantitative evaluation of exposure embeddings.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, exposure conditioning, degradation/restoration networks, filtering, losses and three-stage training remain substantively unchanged. HRBP is renamed HRBA. Newly evaluated conditioning alternatives are experimental comparators, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Restoration coverage remains REDS-ME, REDS-RE, GoPro and the same real-world examples, with unchanged exposure ranges and upscaling task. v2 adds an auxiliary exposure-level classification evaluation of existing ETE embeddings in Section S4.1; it introduces no new restoration dataset or domain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands comparisons testing the exposure-conditioning contribution: Table 4 adds a capacity-matched no-ETE model, Table 5 compares three alternative conditioning designs, and Table S2 adds FGDF without ETM alongside CDF. VRT is newly evaluated in Tables 1–2. Conversely, the FGDF-based upsampling comparator from v1 Table 5 is removed.

E3.justification: Existing restoration splits, metrics and training settings remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial controlled evaluation designs: capacity matching, interventions on guidance while holding video inputs fixed, separate transition-frame reporting, and cosine-similarity k-NN evaluation with k=5. It also specifies a 10-frame, 180×320 memory comparison. These are added protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds capacity-controlled and alternative-conditioning ablations, temporally corrupted guidance tests, quantitative embedding separability, and an unconditioned-FGDF control. The kernel-response visualization becomes bidirectional, testing both short- and long-exposure inputs. The existing fixed-input sensitivity analysis is retained and relocated, while the FGDF upsampling ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Section S4.1 newly reports five-fold cross-validation for estimating exposure-classification accuracy. This does not establish repeated restoration-training runs. Neither version reports restoration seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Headline restoration scores remain unchanged, but substantial diagnostic results are added. The capacity-matched no-ETE model scores 29.88 dB on REDS-RE versus 30.13 for the full model; random wrong-level guidance yields 29.47 dB. ETE classification reaches 92.0%, and the new memory comparison reports 20.5 GB for VRT versus 6.2 GB for FMA-Net++. New comparator rows are added, while the 29.29 dB FGDF-upsampling result is removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds precise mathematical definitions of indexed high-frame-rate averaging and exposure duty cycles in Equations S2–S3. The continuous motion/exposure model and training losses already appear in v1's supplement and are largely relocated or restated. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the benchmark framing from realistic capture conditions to controlled exposure-duration variation. The central claims about parallel temporal modeling, exposure-conditioned restoration, benchmark performance, efficiency and real-world generalization remain. Reordering and consolidating the contribution list does not establish a new method contribution.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges that capacity explains much of the fixed-exposure PSNR gain, while exposure conditioning retains benefits under changing exposure. It distinguishes fixed-input guidance tolerance from failures under temporal guidance corruption and softens the interpretation of interpolation to unseen exposures. Camera-model exclusions become more explicit, but v1's separate discussion of 2D-flow failures under rotation and non-rigid motion is removed.

D1.justification: v2 specifies synthesis indexing, the 80-frame interval at 1920 fps, exact exposure duty cycles and random-walk pseudocode. These clarify the existing generation pipeline rather than establish changed data generation. Core hardware and hyperparameters are retained. Some details disappear, including v1's explicit GoPro bicubic-preprocessing statement and expanded refinement/attention equations.

R1.justification: VRT was already cited, but v2 explicitly acknowledges its sequence-level parallelism and distinguishes FMA-Net++ through computational and memory efficiency. Swin Transformer and Digital Image Warping are added, while several low-light and blur-synthesis references are removed. VRT's preprint-to-publication update is bibliographic rather than a newly cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten, HRBP terminology becomes HRBA throughout, and method exposition is reorganized. Physical-model and loss material move into the main text; the standalone FGDF section is merged into network descriptions. The supplement is extensively restructured into Sections S1–S6.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column presentation, with extensively resized and relocated figures and reformatted metric columns. Exposure examples and analyses move into the main text; kernel visualizations are redesigned and combined with t-SNE. New tables, a confusion matrix and algorithm display are added, while the training-stage schematic is removed. Most qualitative restoration images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens attribution of the central exposure-conditioning contribution. Unlike v1's unequal-capacity and CDF-only comparisons, the matched-capacity and unconditioned-FGDF controls, conditioning alternatives and guidance interventions test competing explanations directly. The revised interpretation acknowledges the capacity confound and defines the benchmark scope more accurately. Removing the upsampling ablation and flow-limitations discussion reduces completeness, but these losses are outweighed by the stronger controlled evidence and more qualified conclusions.
